conditions: For redefinition the formal parameter lists must match. When the inherited procedure and extension type are exported, the redefinition must also be exported.
The caret form is scoped to a receiver parameter and its base-type procedure binding.
limitations: This describes rule-level selection in the named report. Dispatch implementation, layout and error behavior require additional evidence.

triggers: Reassess an edition or source correction, changed evidence bytes, new contrary designer evidence, or change to the base Oberon identity.

statement: The Oberon-2 report describes inherited procedure bindings on record extensions. An extension can redefine a binding with a procedure of the same name and matching formal parameters. Ordinary selection uses the receiver designator's dynamic type, and the caret form on a receiver parameter selects the base-type binding.
